campaign.environment: bd v1.3.1 in scratch workspaces bound to a throwaway dolt sql-server on 127.0.0.1:62888 (stopped after the campaign); isolated HOME; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (bd metrics off); no network services.

summary.description: Phase T t-7 full campaign over bead attach / by-path pour (ADR-0023) and render --append: 9 confirmed bugs promoted as ignored regressions.

workers.target: ADR-0023 negative contract (id, scope, relation, conflict rows), path confinement and symlinks, render --append failures, exit 3 vs exit 2
workers.fuzz_run_description: ADR-0023 negative contract (id, scope, relation, conflict rows), path confinement and symlinks, render --append failures, exit 3 vs exit 2
workers.context_text: 285 recorded checks (~250 sc-compose invocations) on bd v1.3.1 workspaces bnda..bndd. Every refusal left bd byte-identical (list + dep list snapshots). No timeouts, panics or hangs. 18 first-pass harness-expectation errors were rescored. Not testable on APFS: non-UTF-8 file names.

findings.minimal_template: wf/m.formula.toml.j2: formula = "m" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "A"
findings.expected_oracle: A relative template resolves against working_directory, so the render succeeds from any cwd (ADR-0021 line 207 'All paths resolve relative to working_directory'; help bead request table).
findings.observed_result: Exit 3 BEADS_TEMPLATE_PATH_INVALID 'invalid template path: wf/m.formula.toml.j2'. Succeeds only when cwd == working_directory. origin/develop behaves the same (pre-existing). Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0021 paths paragraph; help bead request table; ADR-0023 Authorization and confinement
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed; the contract already states the rule.
findings.root_cause: validate_request canonicalizes request.template (and normalize_output the rendered_formula) as given, so relative paths resolve against the process cwd.
findings.recommended_fix: Join relative template/rendered_formula onto the canonical working_directory before canonicalizing and confining.

workers.target: metamorphic and differential relations: attach twice == once, relation order, CRLF revision, preview == apply, Phase R registry pour vs origin/develop, CLI vs Python receipts, concurrency, determinism
workers.fuzz_run_description: metamorphic and differential relations: attach twice == once, relation order, CRLF revision, preview == apply, Phase R registry pour vs origin/develop, CLI vs Python receipts, concurrency, determinism
workers.context_text: Workspaces difa..difg. Python binding built from head stood in for the Rust library (the optional scratch cargo harness was skipped to avoid writing outside the campaign dir). Concurrent render --append (8x25, 8x25 at 70 KB, 16x10) produced exact counts and no interleaving. CLI and Python receipts agreed in 37/37 cases.

findings.minimal_template: formula = "re g0" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "A"
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Decision 1: additive only; Phase R requests parse unchanged. Baseline accepts these requests (exit 0 render/validate/registry preview-pour).
findings.observed_result: Head: exit 3 BEADS_REQUEST_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED 'invalid graph formula ...; follow ADR-0023' for every operation, including render, which never uses the name. formula_name "" now gives deserialization failure instead of BEADS_FORMULA_NAME_REQUIRED on pour. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator, head vs baseline.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Decision 1 and Consequences; ADR-0021 FormulaNameRequired
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: either keep the grammar and amend ADR-0021/0023 (documenting the breaking change), or confine the grammar to the uses that need it (registry path, graph metadata).
findings.root_cause: Commit e1b5168 made BeadComposeRequest.formula_name a validating FormulaName newtype, so serde rejects names outside [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* during request parsing.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate formula_name only where it becomes a path or bd argument, with a stable code, and keep Phase R parsing unchanged; or record the break in an ADR.

findings.minimal_template: formula = "x" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "A {{{ tag }}}"
findings.minimal_input: request k: ref race<k>, compose_variables {"tag":"T<k>"}, rendered_formula <ws>/build/x.formula.toml
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Atomic apply and Revision: each request's beads come from its own rendered text; GraphApplyFailed means bd wrote nothing.
findings.observed_result: Coordinator repro (3 trials): trial 1: a failed receipt (GraphApplyFailed, 'nothing was written') whose own bd create returned ids for the other request's plan; trial 2: a succeeded receipt for ref race20 created a bead titled 'A T21', i.e. the other request's content. Worker saw cross-contamination in 27/27 trials. Deterministic regression via a path-honest fake bd.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Decision 6, Graph plan, Revision, Errors (GraphApplyFailed); UC-9
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed for the invariant; if a shared rendered_formula is to be unsupported, document and refuse it.
findings.root_cause: graph::run re-reads rendered_formula from disk and bd cooks it by path, and PendingCreate::execute writes then applies the fixed path <rendered_formula>.graph.json, so concurrent requests sharing the path race on both files.
findings.recommended_fix: Hash and cook the bytes this request rendered (private copy), and write the plan to a per-invocation path or hold a lock across render-cook-apply.

workers.target: request JSON shapes; Unicode/control characters in parent, ref, step ids, relation endpoints and metadata; render --append records
workers.fuzz_run_description: request JSON shapes; Unicode/control characters in parent, ref, step ids, relation endpoints and metadata; render --append records
workers.context_text: Workspaces shpa..shpc. Request-shape errors exit 3 before any bd call; Unicode/control text round-trips literally into bd; re-runs up to 33 steps are idempotent; --append framing, newline and not-object refusals leave the destination byte-identical. Three harness-oracle mistakes were corrected.

findings.minimal_template: UC-8 loop: formula = "batch" ... {% for i in range(1, count + 1) %}[[steps]] id = "item_{{{ i }}}" ... needs = ["item_{{{ i - 1 }}}"]{% endfor %}
findings.expected_oracle: FR-23.5 / ADR-0023 UC-4, UC-5: re-running an attach whose beads all exist succeeds and writes nothing; UC-8 generates many steps; no step limit is documented.
findings.observed_result: First attach creates 36 beads; every re-run or preview-attach exits 2 with BEADS_PROCESS_OUTPUT_LIMIT ('Beads Attach output exceeded the 65536-byte capture limit') and no receipt. Threshold ~34 minimal steps (fewer with metadata). The 500-step attach fails even on its first run (bd show stderr for 500 missing ids ~101 KB) and a 500-step graph preview-pour fails on bd cook --json (78 KB). Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator at count=36.
findings.requirement_trace: FR-23.5, FR-23.6; ADR-0023 UC-4, UC-5, UC-8, UC-9, Conflict rules
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed for re-run; if a step ceiling remains, document it in ADR-0023 and the bead manual.
findings.root_cause: GraphReader::issues issues one `bd show <parent> <every planned id> --json`; bd v1.3.1 prints ~1.9 KB per existing bead, beyond runner PROCESS_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES (64 KiB per stream). The cook --json read hits the same cap for large formulas.
findings.recommended_fix: Batch bd show reads, and size the capture limit for graph reads (or stream-parse) so attach scales to the documented use cases.

findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Conflict rules / Relation validation: a missing parent is BEADS_GRAPH_PARENT_NOT_FOUND and a missing bead: endpoint is GraphRelationInvalid(bead_not_found). BeadId only requires non-empty, no whitespace.
findings.observed_result: Exit 2 failed BEADS_GRAPH_READ_FAILED; argv ['bd','show','--help','--help.inj-a',...] and ['bd','show','--db=/nonexistent',...]: bd parsed the ids as options and, for --db=, opened a different database. Controls with ordinary missing ids give the documented codes. Reproduced 3/3 per variant by the coordinator. No write is reachable.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Conflict rules, Relation validation; BeadId contract
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed.
findings.root_cause: Request ids are spliced into `bd show <ids...> --json` and `bd dep list <id> --json` with no `--` separator.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass ids after `--` (bd v1.3.1 accepts it) or reject bead ids starting with '-' at the BeadId boundary.

findings.expected_oracle: help render 'Appending JSON records' step 2: the object is parsed and re-serialized and only its key order may differ; FR-7 render --append.
findings.observed_result: Exit 0; appended {"amount":0.1,"id":1.2345678901234568e+22}. Integers above u64 become lossy floats, long decimals round, 1e2 -> 100.0, -0 -> -0.0. Plain render passes the body unchanged. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator; --append does not exist on origin/develop.
findings.requirement_trace: FR-7 render --append; FR-8a; help render 'Appending JSON records'
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed; if normalization is intended, the manual must say so.
findings.root_cause: append_json_record parses into serde_json::Value without arbitrary_precision and re-serializes.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate the object but keep the original number tokens (arbitrary_precision or RawValue plus minification).

findings.minimal_template: main.formula.toml.j2: formula = "inc" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / @<frag/common.toml.j2> / [[steps]] id = "local" ...; frag/common.toml.j2: [[steps]] id = "shared" title = "Shared step"
findings.expected_oracle: help bead 'Shared step blocks': include fragments with sc-compose's @<path> include syntax; FR-23.1 (structure from loops, conditionals, includes); FR-3.
findings.observed_result: Exit 0 but the rendered formula keeps the literal line '@<frag/common.toml.j2>'; the same text through plain `sc-compose render` expands the include. A later preview-attach fails with BEADS_COOK_FAILED. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator; origin/develop renders the same.
findings.requirement_trace: FR-23.1, FR-3, bead manual 'Shared step blocks', ADR-0023 step_construct guidance
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed.
findings.root_cause: render_formula calls Renderer::render_named on the raw template text and bypasses sc-composer's include-expansion pipeline.
findings.recommended_fix: Run include expansion (confined to working_directory) before rendering bead templates.

findings.expected_oracle: FR-8: diagnostics carry a human-readable message; RenderFailed has a cause message.
findings.observed_result: Exit 2, BEADS_RENDER_FAILED, render stage stderr_excerpt and stdout_excerpt empty; text mode prints only 'stage Render: failed (BEADS_RENDER_FAILED)'. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator; same on baseline.
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed.
findings.root_cause: The receipt built for a render failure drops RenderFailed.message.
findings.recommended_fix: Record the render error message in the render stage's stderr_excerpt, as graph stages do via record_error.

findings.minimal_template: formula = "g" / version = 1 / type = "workflow" / [[steps]] id = "a" title = "T a" needs = ["a"]
findings.minimal_input: preview_attach under an existing epic, ref gcx
findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Errors: GraphApplyFailed carries bd's failure cause so the caller can fix it.
findings.observed_result: Exit 2 BEADS_GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED with message 'graph apply failed (Some(1)): {; [argv]': the cause is '{', the first line of bd's pretty-printed JSON; the real error (blocking dependency cycle) appears only in stdout_excerpt. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator.
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed.
findings.root_cause: process_failure_cause falls back to stdout and short_cause takes its first non-empty line.
findings.recommended_fix: Parse bd's JSON error object (the `error` field) before falling back to the first line.

findings.expected_oracle: ADR-0023 Errors: GraphApplyFailed carries bd's failure cause so the caller can fix it.
findings.observed_result: Exit 2 BEADS_GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED with message 'graph apply failed (Some(1)): {; [argv]': the cause is '{', the first line of bd's pretty-printed JSON; the real error (blocking dependency cycle) appears only in stdout_excerpt. Reproduced 3/3 by the coordinator.
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new ADR needed.
findings.root_cause: process_failure_cause falls back to stdout and short_cause takes its first non-empty line.
findings.recommended_fix: Parse bd's JSON error object (the `error` field) before falling back to the first line.

findings.observed_result: An invalid ref (e.g. 'a.b', '', 33 chars) gives exit 3 BEADS_REQUEST_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED, while the ADR-0023 Id rule and Errors table say GraphIdInvalid, refused, exit 2. The ADR also makes GraphRef a serde try_from newtype and classifies serde failures as exit 3, so it contradicts itself.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Id rule, Errors table, Request errors paragraph; FR-23.10
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: amend the ADR row/manual or map the serde error to GraphIdInvalid.

findings.observed_result: A duplicate key in the appended object is silently collapsed to the last value; bead compose_variables also accept duplicate keys silently, unlike bead_variables. No documented rule.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: refuse or document last-wins.

findings.observed_result: --append follows a final-component symlink (and a dangling one creates the target), like --output. No contract on symlinks for plain render.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead.

findings.observed_result: A graph-mode preview-pour with rendered_formula outside working_directory writes the file and runs bd cook --dry-run before refusing with BEADS_OUTPUT_OUTSIDE_WORKING_DIR at resolve_active_registry; this follows the Phase R registry exception (mode known only after bd where). The refusal code differs from baseline (BEADS_FORMULA_OUTSIDE_ACTIVE_REGISTRY).
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Pour mode selection; ADR-0021 paths
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new doc needed; optional follow-up to refuse before writing.

findings.observed_result: A pre-existing <rendered>.graph.json symlink is refused with BEADS_OUTPUT_PATH_SYMLINK; the outside target is untouched and no bd create runs. Confinement holds.
findings.requirement_follow_up: None.

findings.observed_result: Unknown request and relation fields (e.g. misspelled 'relatoins') are silently ignored, so misspelled relations drop edges without error.
findings.requirement_trace: ADR-0023 Request errors; ADR-0021 request contract
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead (deny_unknown_fields would change Phase R parsing).

findings.observed_result: render --append (and --output) without --json also prints the rendered body to stdout; pre-existing for --output.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead.

findings.observed_result: Concurrent attaches with distinct refs and distinct rendered paths: most fail BEADS_GRAPH_APPLY_FAILED with Dolt 'Error 1213 (40001) serialization failure'; nothing partial is written and re-runs succeed, as the ADR's recovery says.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Optional: document retry for parallel callers.

findings.observed_result: In 1 of 9 trials two identical concurrent attaches both reported nodes 'created'; final bd state equals one attach (no duplicates). Nondeterministic; ADR race paragraph says bd refuses the second plan.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: reword the ADR race paragraph.

findings.observed_result: Permuting relations keeps provenance inputs identical and re-attach is existing (8/8); receipt edges and plan bytes follow request order, which the contract allows ('in plan order').
findings.requirement_follow_up: None.

findings.observed_result: pour_authorization 'yes' gives BEADS_POUR_AUTH_INVALID on head (correct per ADR-0021) vs BEADS_REQUEST_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED on baseline: an intended fix.
findings.requirement_follow_up: None.

findings.observed_result: A TOML formula with lone-CR line endings is refused by bd's TOML parser (BEADS_COOK_FAILED, nothing written); CRLF in TOML/JSON and lone CR in JSON keep the revision (32/32).
findings.requirement_follow_up: None.

findings.observed_result: An undefined {{{ var }}} renders silently: empty in TOML templates, 'null' in JSON templates (TOML/JSON asymmetry); failures surface later as cook or step_graph errors. Plain render warns. No normative rule for bead templates.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: strict undefined or receipt warning.

findings.observed_result: parent containing NUL gives exit 2 BEADS_PROCESS_ARGUMENT_INVALID (no receipt) rather than a request error; other controls give PARENT_NOT_FOUND. BeadId only forbids whitespace.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead: reject control characters in BeadId.

findings.observed_result: compose_variables {"n": 12345678901234567890123} renders as 12345678901234568000000.0 in the formula (same root cause as FUZZ-017: no arbitrary_precision). No documented numeric contract for bead inputs.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead.

findings.observed_result: Macro output interpolated with {{{ ... | safe }}} is TOML-string-escaped again, so macros cannot emit step blocks. No contract for macros.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Decision owner team-lead.

findings.subsystem: Jinja syntax in literal Beads text
findings.observed_result: Literal '{#' or '{%' in bead text fails render (Jinja blocks/comments remain active, ADR-0021); {{ x }} literals survive render, attach and graph pour (FR-23.1 verified in bd).
findings.requirement_follow_up: Optional manual note: use {% raw %}.
